about.title: Rancho Palos Verdes Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Rancho Palos Verdes households rely on everyday products — from kitchen appliances to power tools to items ordered online and delivered along corridors like Palos Verdes Drive S and Hawthorne Boulevard. When a product fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing error, or a missing warning, the harm can be sudden and serious. California law generally allows an injured person to pursue a strict liability claim, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective and caused injury, not on proving the manufacturer was careless. That distinction matters for families in Rancho Palos Verdes trying to sort out medical bills after an incident involving a faulty appliance, vehicle part, tool, or consumer good. whyChoose.title: What Strict Liability Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability standard, showing the product was defective and caused your injury can be enough — you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable for a defective product, which may widen the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: Keeping the defective product, its packaging, and any receipts intact can be critical evidence — an attorney can advise on how to protect it properly.

items.question: What counts as a product defect under California law?
items.answer: There are generally three types: a design defect (the product is inherently unsafe even if made correctly), a manufacturing defect (something went wrong during production), or a warning defect (inadequate instructions or safety labels). Any of these may support a strict liability claim if it caused your injury. An independent attorney can help identify which type applies to your situation.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: No — that's the key feature of strict liability in California. You typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your harm, not that the company acted carelessly. This can simplify certain aspects of a claim compared to a standard negligence case.

items.question: I was hurt by a product near Hawthorne Boulevard in Rancho Palos Verdes — what should I do first?
items.answer: Seek medical care first, then try to preserve the product exactly as it was when the injury happened, including packaging and any receipts. Take photos if you can, and avoid discarding or repairing the item. From there, LawProactive can connect you with an independent attorney, free of charge, to review the details.
